For he first built a church at Alexandria, and in that city was the first preacher and bishop. He was also named by another name, John. Some assert that he was crowned with martyrdom; Jerome, however, affirms that he passed to heaven in the peace of the Church. His deposition is celebrated on the seventh day before the Kalends of May.

55. LUKE, who is interpreted 'raising up' or 'rising up', the third evangelist, a Syrian by nation, of Antioch, whose praise is sung in the Gospel, a scribe and physician by art, a disciple of the apostles, who afterwards followed Paul until his confession, serving the Lord without blame. For he never had a wife or children; a physician of bodies and of souls. For he wrote two books of spiritual medicine, that is, the Gospel, in the regions of Achaia in the time of Paul, which Gospel the apostle Paul says is his own, for he says: 'according to my Gospel'. The other book, which is called the Acts of the Apostles, he wrote for the holy Theophilus, bishop of Antioch. He died at seventy-four years of age in Bethany, full of the Holy Spirit; he was afterwards translated to Constantinople in the twentieth year of the emperor Constantine, with the relics of the blessed apostle Andrew; his deposition is celebrated on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of November.

56. BARNABAS, also called Joseph, by nation of Cyprus, a city founded by Cyrus king of the Persians, obtained the apostleship among the Gentiles with the apostle Paul. Then, on account of the disciple John, who is also called by the surname Mark, he was separated from Paul, yet as an apostle he nonetheless carried out the work of evangelical preaching laid upon him.

57. TIMOTHY, bishop of the Ephesians, from the city of the Trientii, of a Greek, that is, heathen, father, but a Jewish mother, that is, Eunice, as the apostle Paul relates, saying: 'For faith dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and it is certain that [it is] also in you.' He was a disciple of the apostle Paul and his spiritual son, whom that same apostle Paul took with him as a boy as his own; he remained chaste and a virgin, and he rests at Ephesus on the mountain called Pion, by the great shore.

58. TITUS, disciple of the apostle Paul and his son in baptism, a Greek by nation, and the only one from the Gentiles circumcised by the apostle Paul after [receiving] the Gospel; the aforesaid apostle left him to build up the churches of Crete, and having died there in peace, he rests buried.

59. Saint STEPHEN, full of grace, a worthy deacon, and the first martyr after Christ, nephew of Zacchaeus and son of Simon. Stephen was a great soldier, famous in lineage, and shone in beauty; yet more famous in faith and signs, he was radiant to the world. He read the Gospel, he understood the Gospel, he preached the Gospel, he fulfilled the Gospel, he proclaimed Christ perfectly to the peoples, he overcame the synagogues in wisdom, he worked great signs among the people. Filled with the Holy Spirit, he conquered the dogs barking against him, he saw the heavens opened, and beheld Jesus standing at the right hand of the power of God. He sang the holy Scriptures wisely in Jerusalem, and diligently taught his Jewish brethren about the law of God; he rebuked with confidence the hard of heart and the unbelieving; filled with charity, he gently chastised those who did not believe. The enemies of God, seeing these things, gnashed at him with their teeth; the enemies of God, hearing these things, sought how they might kill him; frenzied and raging, filled with fury, like dogs they barked against the saint; lying false witnesses shouted; the wretches condemned the soldier of Christ to death; stiff-necked and cruel of heart, they gathered stones, and dragging Saint Stephen out beyond the city, they stoned him. They stoned, he prayed; they hurled hailstorms of rocks upon him, he joyfully bent his knees to his Maker; they slaughtered him with accursed hands, but he shone full of the ardour of charity; they, foolish companions of Satan, raged against the saint, he, the saint, sang earnestly to the supreme Saviour; they, darkened with fury, gnashed their teeth, he shone with an angelic countenance and a bright face; they, the executioners, vied in bringing stones, he truly prayed for pardon for his persecutors; they cruelly broke the head and body of the saint with rocks, he, looking at the Holy One in heaven, said: 'Lord, do not lay this sin against them'; they poured the blood of Saint Stephen upon the ground, he, Saint Stephen, saw the heavens opened and Jesus standing; they tore the sides of Saint Stephen with flints, he steadfastly gave thanks to Christ; they ran raging, being angry, shouting, he cried out to Christ preaching, praying, singing; they mangled the limbs of the greatest soldier with stones, he, the great soldier, commended his spirit to Christ. And so Saint Stephen, on bended knees, praying, fell asleep in Christ. Saint Stephen, as we said before, saw the heavens opened, and entered in. His prayer gave Saul to the Church as a Christian, and laid low [Saul to make him] the eminent and devout preacher Paul, for if Stephen had not prayed then, the Church would not afterwards have had Paul. After this, then, devout men came from the city, and mourned Saint Stephen with great lamentation, and buried his body with great honour. There, by the Lord's gift, great miracles appear even now, and appeared then. His martyrdom is honoured by the world, and is always celebrated on the seventh day before the Kalends of January. His body, after a time, sought in that same place, was found on the Nones of August, where Christ is believed in and adored by countless thousands.
